comment: The launch screen, in one place. Every platform draws the same block --
mark, wordmark, version -- centred on black, so the frame the system
puts up and the first frame Qt paints are the same picture.
The mark sits at the exact centre of the core and the words hang below
it, because Android 12 and later draw their own launch icon dead centre
before the activity exists: putting our mark anywhere else would make it
jump when Qt takes over.
Numbers are pixels at the 1920x1080 reference the interface is drawn
against; the generator supersamples by renderScale and downsamples.
Two Android frames precede any Qt frame, and both are static resources:
the platform's own launch icon (API 31+), then the activity's window
background, which is the layer-list below. Matching those two to each
other is what the eye actually sees.
The core goes in a density bucket rather than nodpi: a nodpi bitmap is
drawn at its natural pixel size and the layer-list's android:width is
ignored, which drew the mark at 206dp instead of the requested size. A
bucketed bitmap is scaled by density/bucket, so its dp size is exact.
systemIconCanvasDp is the box the platform draws its launch icon into.
The documented 288dp is right; an earlier 270 here was fitted to a
measurement of the broken frame above and made the icon 6% too big.

desktop.comment: Core width as a fraction of the viewport's shorter edge.
